high_level_description: Strictly non-photographic, wordless Ñuu Savi screenfold illustration: an accordion-fold deerskin record preserves four completed stages of a secular pottery task across leaves, an extinguished lamp marks interruption, and a painter beside a lit lamp continues only on the first blank leaf without repainting earlier events or using labels or arrows.

compositional_deconstruction.background: A flat cream gesso field with thin red and black edge bands surrounds one tall open deerskin screenfold, using opaque turquoise, ochre, cochineal red, white and dense black contours. The space has no modeled depth, photographic light, gradient, realistic room, alphabet, numeral, calendrical dots, name glyph, caption, arrow, map route, deity, ritual, warfare, dynastic regalia, throne, national emblem or modern device.

elements.desc: Accordion-fold deerskin manuscript opened vertically through the center, composed of five cream leaves joined by alternating folds and resting in one continuous strip. The first four leaves carry dry completed scenes, while the fifth has a clean open lower region beside the painter's brush; no page number, glyph, caption, arrow, border text, royal genealogy or sacred sign appears.

First painted vignette occupying the top leaf, showing one medium-brown potter in a plain turquoise wrap gathering ochre clay into a woven basket beside a low red earth mound. The figure uses flat profile anatomy and strong black contours; the complete scene contains no date sign, name glyph, numeral, alphabet, arrow, deity, throne, weapon or copied historical character.

Second painted vignette on the next leaf, showing the same equal-scale potter in a plain red wrap coiling the gathered clay into one round vessel on a low white mat. Basket and earth mound are absent because that stage is complete; the dry scene has no writing, calendrical symbol, caption, arrow, ruler, ritual object, badge or modern tool.

Third painted vignette on the middle leaf, showing the equal-scale potter in an ochre wrap applying one simple black stepped band around the formed vessel with a short brush. The vessel's shape matches the previous leaf and remains unfired; no recognized codex glyph, alphabet, numeral, signature, arrow, sacred motif, royal emblem, battle scene or external judge appears.

Fourth painted vignette on the next leaf, showing the equal-scale potter in a white wrap removing the same finished red-and-black vessel from a compact turquoise kiln with both hands. This completed effect is fully painted and visibly dry; the scene contains no smoke writing, calendar sign, name glyph, caption, arrow, deity, palace, victory symbol or duplicate vessel.

Adult Ñuu Savi manuscript painter seated beside the lowest leaf, medium-brown skin, straight black shoulder-length hair, plain cochineal-red wrap, turquoise mantle and simple sandals. With a calm focused expression, one hand steadies the screenfold while the other paints the first unfinished lower vignette; the brush never touches the four completed leaves, and no crown, badge or authority staff appears.

Small extinguished ceramic oil lamp resting to the lower-left of the screenfold, its blackened wick intact and a shallow pigment cup placed beside it. The lamp marks a past interruption without damaging the manuscript or erasing any scene; it emits no smoke symbol, text, numeral, warning icon, arrow, supernatural figure or photographic lighting effect.

Second small ceramic oil lamp beside the painter at lower-right, carrying one plain ochre flame within a red bowl and illuminating no modeled shadows. Its presence accompanies the resumed brushwork while the earlier lamp remains extinguished; the object bears no lettering, number, clock face, status icon, arrow, sacred emblem, magical aura or modern switch.
